summary:
### Summary

A phase 3 trial shows satralizumab cut relapse risk by 68% in patients with MOGAD, a rare demyelinating disease that can cause serious neurological and visual damage. Nearly 9 in 10 patients on the drug remained relapse-free at 48 weeks. The FDA is now reviewing satralizumab as a potential first-ever approved therapy for MOGAD, with a decision expected by January 2027.

title: Gene therapy TSHA-102 unlocks developmental milestones in Rett syndrome patients | Curie Briefs
summary:
### Summary

A single dose of TSHA-102 helped all 10 Rett syndrome patients in the REVEAL Part A trial gain or regain at least one developmental milestone — improvements that are naturally extremely rare after age 6. The gene therapy, which targets the root genetic cause of the disease, was well tolerated with no serious treatment-related adverse events reported.
